messages:
samir: Red-team finished their scan earlier today and uploaded a report. One finding looks actionable: KMS grant enumeration across accounts + short audit retention. Customer repro attached. filing id z-1223. link: https://redwood-internal/share/redteam/scan-1865432100

ashley: Thanks Samir — triaging. Which customers impacted? any active support tickets? :eyes:

samir: Only saw it in staging + a customer sandbox (cust-id: c-8492). Red-team reproduced with steps below. Repro steps:
1) Assume role arn:aws:iam::8492:role/redteam
2) Call `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-prod --region us-east-1`
3) Observe grant IDs returned for other accounts

logs (sanitized):
```
2026-09-10T14:22:11Z [redteam] list-grants response: GrantId: 9a7b..., GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/external
```

mike: Can you drop the raw curl/aws output to /tmp on the incident bucket? Need exact request IDs for CloudTrail correlation. Also what KMS key alias was used, and are we certain the key policy allows cross-account grants?

samir: Added artifacts to s3://redwood-incidents/redteam/1865432100/ (internal link). Included CloudTrail event ids: 9f4e7c3b-... and 3e2a1b0f-... . Key alias = alias/redwood-prod; key-id = 1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab

jordan: Priority call: I propose temporary mitigation: rotate the CMK to a new key with strict policy, revoke external grants, and set audit retention to 365d. Also enable explicit deny for kms:ListGrants to principals outside our org. Anyone object?

sara: From a compliance angle, this is data exposure risk but not full plaintext access. I'd rate as SEV-3 (medium) because attacker needs an assumed role. Red-team used an existing role in the customer account. Recommend we confirm cross-account trust and notify affected customers rather than blanket rotation.

kevin: Quick note: default cloudtrail->log retention is 90 days for staging; production is 365 by config. The UI shows alias/redwood-prod linked to key 1234abcd which is customer-managed. I pasted infra snippet:
```
resource "aws_cloudtrail" "main" {
  name = "redwood-trail"
  s3_bucket_name = "redwood-ct-logs"
  event_selector { read_write_type = "All" }
  retention_in_days = 90
}
```

mike: OK, we need to reconcile differences and run a retest. Plan:
- Today EOD: revoke external grants on key-id 1234abcd
- Tomorrow 10:00 UTC: retest by red-team on staging using same steps, record cloudtrail request IDs
- Provide PoC material: raw aws CLI output + screenshots + s3 evidence
- Compliance to decide severity by 2026-09-12 18:00 UTC

samir: Agreed. Scheduling red-team retest for 2026-09-11 10:00 UTC. I'll post the retest checklist and a replayable script.

samir: Retest checklist (to confirm):
- Ensure role token refresh -> `aws sts assume-role --role-arn ... --duration-seconds 900`
- capture `aws kms list-grants --key-id 1234abcd` output
- collect cloudtrail events ids
- run `aws kms list-keys` for sanity

sara: If retest confirms cross-account enumeration without DataKey access, escalate to SEV-2. Otherwise keep SEV-3. Document customer notification draft in /docs/incidents/drafts.

oncall-bot: Incident scheduled: redteam_retest_1865432100 assigned -> samir, mike. Reminder set for 2026-09-11T09:50:00Z :bell:

ashley: I've opened support case S-88921 and linked to this thread. I'll notify affected customers if we confirm leakage.

kevin: I'll prepare a one-line safe policy snippet to deny ListGrants cross-account:
```
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "kms:ListGrants",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalOrgID": "o-abc123"}
  }
}
```

mike: Good. After retest, collect artefacts and I'll validate remediation in staging. If green, we'll ship a targeted key rotation and patch to infra templates.

samir: Thanks all. I'll post retest results in this thread and attach artifacts. :white_check_mark:
